\\[2pt] \footnotesize Same one-minute windows, sessions, and partitions for every row: ten session-wise splits as in Table~\ref{tab:splits}; four folds that each hold out one synthetic session per kind and a quarter of the genuine sessions, repeated over ten seeds; and leave-one-kind-out (LOKO) with the genuine test sessions of the first split. Wang et al.\ features follow their seven mouse groups (43 values) with keystroke hold and down-down latency summarised by mean and standard deviation; pointer actions are segmented at gaps above 500\,ms, a rule their paper does not specify. Hold times exist in 80\,\% of genuine and 0\,\% of synthetic windows, because the generator emits no \texttt{key\_up}; without them the Wang forest scores $F_1$ 0.975 and LOKO mean 0.647. Its permutation importance is led by \texttt{ata\_move} (0.57), \texttt{ata\_point\_click} (0.47), \texttt{hold\_mean} (0.42). The isolation-forest rows are one-class, trained on genuine windows only. Rules learn nothing; their AUC is that of a binary score.
